myth: The rise of the West is a Western-European story: a few countries dominated because events took place only there.
fact: Configuration of power dates back ~500 years; encounters with the Americas, Africa and Asia were profoundly different; genocide, slavery, colonial plunder and silver funded Western dominance.

myth: Age of Discovery + Enlightenment + Scientific Revolution → Industrial Revolution; 'free' labour shed pre-capitalist shackles.
fact: Slavery, genocide, expropriation of Indigenous land and colonial loot predated and accompanied industrialisation; not minor aberrations.

myth: Capitalism rose from technological innovation, science and 'capitalist rationality.'
fact: 'So-called originary accumulation' was expropriation: loot, not savings. Sugar + enslaved people as paired commodities laid foundations.

myth: The plantation is an archaic, pre-capitalist institution.
fact: Field and factory; integrated cultivation + processing; cost accounting; productivity calculation; modern management; human beings as fixed capital / replaceable machines. 'Unholy marriage of capital with Atlantic chattel slavery.'

myth: Sugar is just a commodity like others.
fact: Sugar was the first global commodity; created the capitalist market; laid foundations of the global financial system; accompanied by a second 'commodity': enslaved people.

myth: Slavery was incidental; capitalism needs 'free' labour.
fact: Capitalism rooted in plantations + enslaved labour; abolition later didn't erase accumulated wealth; institutionalised in finance, property, global division of labour.

myth: Triangular trade is only manufactures ↔ enslaved people ↔ raw materials.
fact: Overlooked commodities too: Indian textiles, saltpetre/gunpowder, guns; colonial loot from India paid for African exports; re-exports; internal slave markets.

myth: Industrial Revolution in Britain created Western hegemony.
fact: Sugar refineries were earliest factory workplaces; reserve currencies (guilder, sterling) & capital predated Industrial Revolution; profits funded industry; 'not even a nail.'

myth: Silver/gold mining is peripheral to capitalism.
fact: Spanish silver (Mexico, Potosí) = 80% world supply 1494–1850; commodity money; financed Europe→Asia; asiento linked slavery to silver & Asian trade; 'singular product most responsible for the birth of world trade was silver.'

myth: Since slavery already existed in Africa, Europeans just tapped existing markets.
fact: West introduced industrial-scale 'production' of enslaved people; transformed domestic slavery; gun-slave-money; ~14–20m seized; demographic catastrophe.

myth: American lands stood empty, waiting for Europeans.
fact: Genocide; land seized; Indigenous peoples destroyed; 'genocidal violence.'

myth: Sugar techniques/enslaved labour are purely European innovations.
fact: Sugar from eastern Mediterranean; Arab/Muslim Andalusia; sugar masters from Egypt/Syria; cane from Levant; two-roller mill possibly from West India; enslaved East Africans in Euphrates; bagasse in Mamluk Egypt; servile/corvée + enslaved labour.
